Petition under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award
1.

The petitioner aged about 17 years and 3 months has sought compensation to the tune of Rs.
5,00,000/ with interest @ 18% per annum from the date of filing of petition till the date of
realization, for the injuries sustained by him in Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on
17.12.2019 at about 10:30 Pm near Phoenix United Mall, Pilibhit Bypass Macp No. 46/20; Fir No.
948/19 Dod: 20.03.2023 Road, Bareilly, Up, involving Truck bearing registration no. Up25Ct
1547 (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 4 in a rash and negligent manner.
2. It is averred in the claim petition that on 17.12.2019 at about 10:30 Pm, the petitioner/injured
was in car with his family members bearing registration no. Dl3Cbr4580 which was lying
parked on the extreme left side of the road with parking lights On.

When the aforesaid car was
standing stationed, offending vehicle which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a
rash and negligent manner, came from backside and hit against the aforesaid car with a great force,
as a result of which, he sustained grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to Shrinath Medicity
Hospital, Up.
Fir No. 948/19, u/s. 279/337/338/427 Ipc was registered at Ps. Izzat Nagar, Up.

It is
further averred that the petitioner was student as well as also giving private tuition and was earning
Rs. 15,000/ per month at the time of accident.

The offending vehicle was found to be owned by
respondent no. 1 & 2 jointly and insured with respondent no.3 i.e. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd during
the period in question.

3. In their joint Ws, the respondent no. 1 & 2 i.e. joint owners of offending vehicle denied the
averments made by the petitioner in his claim petition.

They claimed that the offending vehicle was
being driven by Sh. Umesh Pal Singh/respondent no. 4 at the time of accident.

They further Macp
No. 46/20; Fir No. 948/19 Dod: 20.03.2023 claimed that respondent no. 4 was having valid and
effective driving licence at the time of accident.

It has been further claimed that offending vehicle
was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident and as such, they are not liable to pay any
compensation to the petitioners.

2

4.

In its written statement, the respondent no. 3 has admitted that offending vehicle was insured
with it in the name of respondent no. 1 & 2 at the time of accident.

It has denied the averments made
in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

5. In his written statement, the respondent no. 4 i.e. driver of offending vehicle denied the
averments made by the petitioner in his claim petition.

He claimed that the accident had taken place
due to the negligence of petitioner himself.

He further claimed that he was driving the offending
vehicle very carefully and was also holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
On the basis of these averments, he has prayed for dismissal of claim petition.

6. From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 25.02.2021
by my Ld. Predecessor:

1. Whether the petition is liable to be dismissed as the driver Sh. Umesh Pal Singh (name disclosed
by respondents no. 1 & 2 in their written statement) has not been arrayed as respondent?OPP
2. Whether the injured Abdul Wahid Hussain suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 1

7.12.2019 at about 10:30 PM near Phoenix United Mall, Pilibhit Bypass Road, Bareilly, Uttar Prades within the jurisdiction of PS. Izzat Nagar due to rashness and negligence on the part of driver Sh. Umesh Pal Singh who was driving vehicle bearing registration no. UP25CT1547, jointly owned by Sh. Aslam and Sh. Shanu and insured with Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.?

OPP. 
3. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
4. Relief.
7.
Before proceeding further, it may be noted that vide order dated 04.06.2022, it was directed that the petitioner shall not be entitled to any interest w.e.f. 06.09.2021 till conclusion of PE.
Record shows that PE was concluded on 21.12.2022.

Thus, right to claim interest, if any, by the petitioners has been curtailed from 06.09.2021 till 21.12.2022.
8.
In support of his claim, the petitioner has examined two witnesses i.e. himself as PW1 and PW2 Sh. Wajid Hussain (father of injured) and closed his evidence on 21.12.2022.
On the other hand, no evidence was adduced by any of the respondents.

I have heard the arguments addressed by Ld. Counsel for the petitioner whereas despite grant of opportunity, respondent no. 1,2 & 4 did not come forward to either advance arguments or file their respective written synopsis.
I have also gone through the record.

My findings on the issues are as under:

Counsel for insurance company raised an objection to the maintainability of the claim petition and disputed liability of insurance company to pay the compensation amount in this case as the petitioner had not made the driver of offending vehicle party in the present case.

11. It may be noted here that although initially, driver of offending vehicle was not made party by the petitioner in his claim petitioner, however, after disclosure of the name of the driver of the offending vehicle in the joint written statement filed on behalf of joint owner of the offending vehicle i.e.
respondents no. 1 & 2, petitioner had moved the application u/o 1 Rule 10 r/w Section 151 CPC for leave to implead driver of the offending vehicle as respondent no. 4 in the array of parties.
Accordingly, notice was issued to respondent no. 4 who had filed his separate WS.
MACP No. 46/20; FIR No. 948/19 DOD: 20.03.2023 12.
It is relevant to mention here that firstly, it has nowhere been disputed by insurance company in its WS/reply that offending vehicle was not insured with it at the time of accident.
Secondly, no evidence whatsoever has been led by insurance company on the aspect that there was any breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy by the insured at the time of accident.
Hence, it is beyond dispute that offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no. 3 as on the date of accident.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, I am of the considered opinion that the present claim petition is very much maintainable under the law.
Issue no
. 1 is decided accordingly.
13. For the purpose of this issue, the testimonies of PW1 & PW2 are relevant.
In their respective evidence by way of affidavits (Ex. PW1/A & PW2/A respectively), they both have deposed on the similar lines of averments made in the claim petition.
PW1 Sh. Abdul Wahid Hussain has relied upon the following documents:
S.No. Description of documents Remarks 1. Copy of Aadhaar Card Ex PW1/1 2. Photograph and newspaper Ex. PW1/2(colly) report of the accident 3.
Certified copy of FIR No. Ex. PW1/3(colly) MACP No. 46/20; FIR No. 948/19 DOD: 20.03.2023 5.
Certified copy of injury Ex. PW1/5 Report/Certificate 6.
Medical treatment record, Ex. PW1/6(colly) medical bills of Rs. 39,873.05 with summary 14.
During cross examination on behalf of insurance company, PW1 deposed that he did not remember the date of accident.
He further deposed that he was sitting on the back seat of car at the time of accident.
He further deposed that the car was being driven by his father at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that they had not switched ON the parking lights of their car at the time of accident.
15. PW2 Sh. Wajid Hussain has relied upon the following documents:

During crossexamination on behalf of insurance company, PW2 deposed that at the time of accident, their car was standing on the extreme left side of the road and blinkers of their Car were ON.

He denied the suggestion that at the time of accident, the blinkers of his car were not MACP No.
46/20; FIR No. 948/19 DOD: 20.03.2023 ON.
He deposed that at the time of accident, he was wearing seat belt.
He volunteered that he was at the driver's seat in the car whereas petitioner was sitting on the back seat.
He deposed that he had made call to the police on number 100 after the accident.
He again said some passerby had already made call to the police regarding the accident.

17. It is evident from the testimonies of PW1 & PW2 that the respondents more particularly insurance company could not impeach their testimonies through litmus test of crossexamination and they are found to have successfully withstood the test of crossexamination.

Even otherwise,
PW1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely about the accident.
Moreover, FIR No. 948/19(Ex. PW1/3 colly) is shown to have been registered on the statement of PW2 Sh. Wajid Hussain(father of petitioner) who was accompanying the petitioner at the time of accident.
The contents of said FIR would show that Sh. Wajid Hussain had disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by him as PW2 in the present case.
Thus, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimonies of these witnesses made on oath.
18. As noted above, FIR No. 948/19 (supra) was registered at PS. Izzat Nagar, UP with regard to accident in question.

Copy of said FIR alongwith copy of chargesheet (which are part of criminal case record) would show that FIR was registered on 18.12.2019(accident being caused MACP No.
46/20; FIR No. 948/19 DOD: 20.03.2023 on 17.12.2019 at about 10:30 PM).
Thus, FIR was registered promptly and without any delay.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondents and / or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioner.

19. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no. 4 i.e. driver of the offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he preferred not to enter into witness box during the course of inquiry.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

20. Not only this, the respondent no. 4 namely Sh. Umesh Pal Singh(accused in State case) has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s 279/337/338/427 IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

Apart from above, copy of MLC (Mark PW1/4) of injured prepared at Medicity Hospital, Delhi,
shows that he had been removed to said hospital on 18.12.2019 at 12.06 AM with alleged history of RTA.

On his local examination, he was found to have sustained multiple injuries as MACP No.
46/20; FIR No. 948/19 DOD: 20.03.2023 mentioned therein.
The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in motor vehicular accident.
Again, there is no challenge to the said document from the side of respondents including insurance company.

22. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of pre ponderence of probabilities that he had sustained injuries in road accident which took place on 17.12.2019 at about 10:30 PM near Phoenix United Mall, Pilibhit Bypass Road, Bareilly, UP due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Thus, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
23. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
MEDICAL EXPENSES 24.

The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex. PW1/A) that after the accident, he had been taken to Shrinath MACP No. 46/20; FIR No. 948/19 DOD: 20.03.2023 Medicity Hospital, Pilibhit Bypass Road, Bareilly, UP and thereafter, he was taken to St. Stephen Hospital, Tis Hazari, Delhi.

During his crossexamination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that he did not remember as to who took him to the hospital as he became unconscious after the accident.
He further deposed that he remained admitted for around three days in the hospital.
25. It is relevant to note that the petitioner has relied upon medical bills to the tune of Rs. 39,873.05 only, which are Ex. PW1/6(colly).
It is quite evident that the respondents have not disputed the authenticity and genuineness of the said medical bills during the course of inquiry.
They have also not led any evidence in rebuttal so as to create any doubt on the genuineness of said bills.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs. 40,000/(rounded off) is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

948/19 DOD: 20.03.2023 eye, he could not study properly and thus, suffered loss of studies also.

During his crossexamination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that he was aged about 18 years at the time of accident.
He deposed that he was advised bed rest for about one month by the doctor.
He deposed that he had not suffered any permanent disability in the accident.
He further deposed that he had not placed on record any document to show that he was 12th class pass.
He volunteered that he was doing BCA from IITM, Janakpuri, Delhi.
He denied the suggestion that he was not doing BCA from the said college as he had not placed on record any such document.

He deposed that he used to earn Rs.
7200/ per month from tuitions.
He denied the suggestion that he did not use to take tuitions as he had not filed any document in this regard.

27. The Discharge Summary (which is part of Ex. PW1/6 colly) of Shrinath Medicity Hospital, in respect of petitioner/injured, would reveal that he was admitted in the said hospital on 18.12.2019 and discharged on 20.12.2019.
As per the treatment record, the petitioner had sustained fracture lateral wall of right orbit.

Apart from the aforesaid documents produced by the petitioner, he has failed to file any other medical treatment record in order to show the exact period upto which he had received the medical treatment.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the MACP No.
46/20; FIR No. 948/19 DOD: 20.03.2023 petitioner and in view of the treatment record brought on record, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work atleast for a period of 3 months or so.

28. Apart from the bald statement made by the petitioner that he was earning Rs. 12,000/ to Rs.
15,000/ per month, no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove his monthly income at the time of accident in question.
It may be noted here that father of petitioner has filed copy of 12th class marksheet (Ex. PW2/2) of petitioner in respect of his educational qualification.

In view of the aforesaid document Ex. PW2/2, I am of the view that loss of income of the petitioner has to be assessed while taking the income of a Matriculate person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question The minimum wages of a Matriculate person were Rs. 17,991/ per month as on the date of accident which is 17.12.2019.

Thus, a sum of Rs.
53,973/ (Rs. 17,991/ x 3) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.
PAIN AND SUFFERING 29.

sentences.text: The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/A) that he had sustained grievous injuries i.e. facial trauma (fracture lateral wall of right orbit) in the accident in question.
Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings and mental shock on account of the accident in question.

Keeping in view the medical treatment record of petitioner available on record and the nature of injuries suffered by him, I hereby award a sum of Rs. 75,000/ towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.
LOSS OF GENERAL AMENITIES & ENJOYMENT OF LIFE 31.
As already mentioned above, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries due to the accident.
In the present case, petitioner is a young boy of aged about 18 years at the time of accident.
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.
In view of the nature of injuries suffered by him, I award a notional sum of Rs. 75,000/ towards loss of general amenities and enjoyment of life to the petitioner.

MACP No. 46/20; FIR No. 948/19 DOD: 20.03.2023 CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET &
ATTENDANT CHARGES 32.

The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A that he had spent Rs.
50,000/on conveyance, Rs. 20,000/ each on special diet and attendant charges.
The petitioner has failed to lead any cogent evidence to prove the amount, if any spent on special diet, conveyance and attendant as aforesaid by him.
At the same time, it cannot be overlooked that petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

Thus, he would have taken special rich protein diet for his speedy recovery and would have also incurred considerable amount towards conveyance charges while commuting to the concerned hospital as OPD patient for his regular check up & follow up during the period of his medical treatment.
He would have been definitely helped by some person either outsider or from his family, to perform his daily activities as also while visiting the hospital during the course of his medical treatment.
In these facts and circumstances, I hereby award a notional sum of Rs. 20,000/for conveyance and Rs. 15,000/each for special diet and attendant charges to the petitioner.

Thus, the total compensation is assessed as under:
1. Medical Expenses Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of income Rs. 53,973/
3. Pain and suffering Rs. 75,000/

Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Respondent no. 3/insurance company did not adduce any evidence as it had no statutory defence.
It is nowhere the case of insurance company that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/violated by insured.
Keeping in view the existence of valid insurance policy, respondent no. 3/insurance company becomes liable to pay the compensation amount, as insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured.
Issue no. 2
is decided accordingly.

by respondents no. 1 & 2 in their written statement) has not been arrayed as respondent?OPP
Macp

2. Whether the injured Abdul Wahid Hussain suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 1
7.12.2019 at about 10:30 PM near Phoenix United Mall, Pilibhit Bypass Road, Bareilly, Uttar Prades within the jurisdiction of PS. Izzat Nagar due to rashness and negligence on the part of driver Sh. Umesh Pal Singh who was driving vehicle bearing registration no. UP25CT1547, jointly owned by Sh. Aslam and Sh. Shanu and insured with Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.?
OPP. 
3. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?
22. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of pre ponderence of probabilities that he had sustained injuries in road accident which took place on 17.12.2019 at about 10:30 PM near Phoenix United Mall, Pilibhit Bypass Road, Bareilly, UP due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Secondly, no evidence whatsoever has been led by insurance company on the aspect that there was any breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy by the insured at the time of accident.
Hence, it is beyond dispute that offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no. 3 as on the date of accident.
Moreover, FIR No. 948/19(Ex. PW1/3 colly) is shown to have been registered on the statement of PW2 Sh. Wajid Hussain(father of petitioner) who was accompanying the petitioner at the time of accident.
The contents of said FIR would show that Sh. Wajid Hussain had disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by him as PW2 in the present case.
Thus, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimonies of these witnesses made on oath.
Thus, FIR was registered promptly and without any delay.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondents and / or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioner.
19. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no. 4 i.e. driver of the offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he preferred not to enter into witness box during the course of inquiry.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.
20. Not only this, the respondent no. 4 namely Sh. Umesh Pal Singh(accused in State case) has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s 279/337/338/427 IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.
Thus, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
23. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
In view of the aforesaid document Ex. PW2/2, I am of the view that loss of income of the petitioner has to be assessed while taking the income of a Matriculate person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question The minimum wages of a Matriculate person were Rs. 17,991/ per month as on the date of accident which is 17.12.2019.
Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the matter titled as " Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors."
In the present case, petitioner is a young boy of aged about 18 years at the time of accident.
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.
At the same time, it cannot be overlooked that petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Respondent no. 3/insurance company did not adduce any evidence as it had no statutory defence.
It is nowhere the case of insurance company that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/violated by insured.
Keeping in view the existence of valid insurance policy, respondent no. 3/insurance company becomes liable to pay the compensation amount, as insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured.
